name: Goblin Minion

traits.name: Haha, Missed Me!
traits.text: Whenever an attack misses you, deal 2 psychic damage (ignoring armor).

flavor: The cannon fodder of goblin society: lazy, sneaky, and only slightly more threatening than a thrown boot. Their job? Get in the way, hurl insults, and die hilariously.
notes: Tactics lines are placeholder "xx" in the source; left null.

name: Goblin

traits.name: Haha, Missed Me!
traits.text: Whenever an attack misses you, deal 2 psychic damage (ignoring armor).

flavor: The backbone of any raiding party, especially when it comes to setting up makeshift traps, stealing food, and heckling anything with a pulse.

tactics.easier: Very injured Goblins can run past multiple heroes, and less injured Goblins can remain adjacent to melee heroes rather than running away to same them an action moving.
tactics.harder: If a hero is within Reach 6, run up to them, stab, then run away in hopes of triggering an Opportunity Attack. Goad heroes into it with verbal taunts: "You can't catch me!" feigning fear (especially if you miss, or seeing them survive your best stab) "Ahh! Run awaayy!"

name: Goblin Ratrider

traits.name: Haha, Missed Me!
traits.text: Whenever an attack misses you, deal 2 psychic damage (ignoring armor).

traits.name: CHAAARGE!
traits.text: If you move at least 4 spaces in a straight line, attack with advantage once.

flavor: Riding into battle atop mangy giant rats, these goblins are thrill-seekers and scouts. Their mounts are as diseased and unpredictable as their riders.

tactics.easier: Can stay more stationary or spread their damage around, don't attack Prone targets.
tactics.harder: Hunt down backline and isolated heroes. Stay out of reach of melee heroes, set up powerful attacks for Bugbears when they knock Heroes Prone.

name: Goblin Taskmaster

traits.name: Haha, Missed Me!
traits.text: Whenever an attack misses you, deal 2 psychic damage (ignoring armor).

traits.name: Meat Shield
traits.text: Can force other goblins to Interpose for him.

actions.name: Get in here!
actions.text: Call a goblin minion to the fight.

flavor: Mean enough to boss other goblins around and survive the attempt. They often work under the heel of Bugbears, screaming secondhand orders and threats they usually can't deliver on.

tactics.easier: May "run out" of minions to call to the battlefield or their minions may be out of position to Interpose for them.
tactics.harder: Keep a minion within Interpose range at all times!

name: Nilbog

traits.name: Backwards Chaos
traits.text: Attacks that would hit a Nilbog instead miss, attacks that would miss, hit instead.

traits.name: Neener Neener!
traits.text: When a hero's attack misses a Goblin or when a hero could opportunity attack a Goblin, but doesn't: Deal 4 psychic damage.

flavor: The chosen fools—when one arises, logic dies. Entire warrens descend into laughter, worship, and property damage. Minions throw themselves off ledges in reverence and Taskmasters weep in frustration.

tactics.easier: Stay near heroes with smaller weapons (d4, d6) or Cheats. Keep Goblins at a distance.
tactics.harder: Stay near heroes with larger weapons (d10, d12) who will have a harder time hitting. Constantly move Goblins in and out of melee range.

notes: No actions printed.

name: Bugbear
flavor: Big, brutish, and permanently grumpy, Bugbears are the heavy muscle of Goblin society. They despise noise and disorder—Bugbears tolerate Goblins' antics in exchange for servitude and a steady supply of things to hit.

tactics.easier: Attack from Range or spread damage out. Attack first in a round while heroes can still Interpose & Defend.
tactics.harder: Bugbears are patient ambushers,they can start combat hidden, attacking any hero who has strayed too far from his party, or their back lines.

name: Bugbear Chieftain

traits.name: I want results!
traits.text: Goblins gain +2 speed and advantage on attacks.

actions.name: Cleave
actions.text: (Reach 2) 2d6+10, can also damage a 2nd target within Reach.

flavor: Chieftains rule with fear, iron clubs, and a zero-tolerance policy for goblin antics (except the useful kind). Under their leadership, goblins become surprisingly efficient raiders—at least for a few weeks.

tactics.easier: Use cleave to also strike a goblin that is in your way.
tactics.harder: Target only heroes. Force a goblin to Interpose for you.

name: Krogg, Goblin King
actionsIntro: After each hero’s turn, choose one:

actions.name: Crack Skulls
actions.text: Move 6. Swing a Grappled creature at another creature. Both take 2d6+2 damage, ending the Grapple.

bloodied.text: At 45 HP, Krogg’s damage increases to 2d8+2.

lastStand.text: At 0 HP Krogg is dying! If he takes 20 more damage he dies. Until then, he has Medium Armor.

flavor: All hail Krogg, the Goblin King! Goblins respect Krogg, because when Krogg issues a decree, he does so with his fists. He's not, strictly speaking, of "royal blood", but anyone capable of keeping a Goblins on-task for more than a few minutes deserves the title "King".

tactics.easier: Have the Manglemaul jam after using Crack Skulls. Krogg gets verbally frustrated with the “stupid weapon” it loses the ability to Grapple, or he could spend a turn fixing it.
tactics.harder: Manglemaul may retain the Grappled target, so Crack Skulls can be used again next turn. Or you could also knock heroes Prone after Cracking Skulls. Move more frequently, end your turn out of reach of melee heroes.

notes: Header: "lvl 2 Solo Angry Bugbear"; actions labelled "ACTIONS:". Harder tactic continues in the next column.

name: Vermis & Skittersnack

traits.name: Mangy Rat
traits.text: When Skittersnack is struck, summon 1 giant flea (a d4 minion, on hit: 1 damage).

actionsIntro: After each hero’s turn, alternate using your 2 abilities:

actions.name: Chaaarrge!
actions.text: Move 10 in a straight line, deal 2d6 damage to all in your path (2 spaces wide).

actions.name: Itchy Fleas
actions.text: Move 4. Skittersnack summons 1 giant flea/hero (they act at the end of each round).

bloodied.name: Flea Bitten Varmint!
bloodied.text: At 60 HP Skittersnack summons 3 Giant Fleas per hero.

lastStand.name: Fleas, Please!
lastStand.text: Veris & Skittersnack are dying! 30 more damage and they die. Until then, they perform both actions each turn.

flavor: Vermis is more than a nuisance, he's a menace! And that rat Skittersnack is a bad influence at best. Vermis rides through town at all hours, yelling obscenities and stealing anything he can't eat. Even worse, Skittersnack has started developing a following... of fleas! It's high time someone stopped the duo's reign of terror.

tactics.easier: When using Chaaarrge!, ensure you hit minions, and fewer heroes. Keep giant fleas clumped up or near heroes that can easily use an AoE, so they are easier to eliminate.
tactics.harder: Line up multiple heroes with Chaaarrge! Kill as few of your own minions as possible. Spread out giant fleas so they are harder to kill in large numbers.

notes: Header: "lvl 3 Solo Goblin & Large Rat Cavalry"; no separate size token, size Large inferred from the rat mount. Last Stand misspells "Veris" in source.

groupTraits.name: Nooooo!
groupTraits.text: Whenever an ally within Reach 2 dies, attack once for free.

name: Kobold
flavor: A loyal friend and a tenacious enemy. Unthreatening… until they're surrounded by friends!

tactics.easier: Attack from Range, and stay spread out.
tactics.harder: Keep them close together to maximize Nooooo!

groupTraits.name: Nooooo!
groupTraits.text: Whenever an ally within Reach 2 dies, attack once for free.

name: Kobold Sneak

traits.name: Revenge!
traits.text: When an ally dies, you may move 6 before using your Nooooo! ability.

flavor: A hyperactive blur of speed, dashing around the battlefield.

tactics.easier: Stay on the frontlines, making them likely to die before making use of their ability.
tactics.harder: Keep them away from danger, but always close enough to dash in when an ally dies.

groupTraits.name: Nooooo!
groupTraits.text: Whenever an ally within Reach 2 dies, attack once for free.

name: Kobold Trapper

traits.name: Trap!
traits.text:
When an enemy moves adjacent to you or an ally, they trigger one of your traps! (1/encounter each).
• Trap: BEEES! Deal 5d4 damage (doesn’t miss). Half as much to ALL adjacent creatures.
• Trap: HIDDEN NET! Restrained (escape DC 10).

tactics.easier: Damage (but don't kill) other kobolds with BEES!
tactics.harder: Position yourself to use BEES! to strike multiple heroes, and kill 1 weakened kobold to trigger lots of Nooooo! attacks.

groupTraits.name: Nooooo!
groupTraits.text: Whenever an ally within Reach 2 dies, attack once for free.

notes: Flavour is placeholder "XX" in the source; left null.

name: Kobold Clanger

traits.name: CLANG!
traits.text: Allies who hear your clanging, roll 1 additional die WHENEVER they attack.

flavor: The height of kobold fashion: butket on head, frying pan armor and ladle drumsticks. The louder the noise, the better the party.

tactics.easier: Wander close into battle. Being Grappled or knocked Prone could temporarily silence them.
tactics.harder: Keep them in the back lines and running away from heroes. Never end your turn within reach of a melee hero, or without cover from ranged attacks!

groupTraits.name: Nooooo!
groupTraits.text: Whenever an ally within Reach 2 dies, attack once for free.

notes: Flavour and tactics continue at the top of the next column.

name: Kobold Denwarden

traits.name: Hold!
traits.text: Adjacent allies gain Medium Armor.

flavor: Equal parts big brother and parental figure, Denwardens would do anything to protect their kin.

tactics.easier: Keep them separated from allies, and spread their attacks between heroes.
tactics.harder: Place them in the center of Kobold lines, increasing the power of both "Hold!" and "Nooooo!"

groupTraits.name: Nooooo!
groupTraits.text: Whenever an ally within Reach 2 dies, attack once for free.

name: Kobold Dragon Relic

traits.name: Time-Worn Stone
traits.text: Ignores non-critical damage. Take a max of 1 damage per turn.

traits.name: Frenzied Devotion
traits.text: Kobolds roll d8s instead of d4s and take a max of 10 damage from attacks.

flavor: When a kobold clan finds a suitable effigy for their devotion, a fanatical fervor overtakes them. This is often bad news for their neighbors.

tactics.easier: Spread Kobolds out, making the Relic easy to attack and reducing the times each Kobold can attack. Ignore the 1 damage/turn limit.
tactics.harder: A very special relic could also double the Reach of Nooooo! Or it could also trigger whenever the relic is attacked.

groupTraits.name: Nooooo!
groupTraits.text: Whenever an ally within Reach 2 dies, attack once for free.

notes: Header: "Lvl 3x (triple the lvl of all nearby Kobolds), Large". No actions printed.

name: Narbles & His Stack of Friends

traits.name: Noooo!
traits.text: When Bloodied and at Last Stand, the top kobold is defeated and falls off. The rest immediately move and make an attack for free.

bloodied.text: At 34hp, Toads is defeated. Narbles grabs his frying pan and uses it as a shield (gain Medium Armor) and each turn: Stab. Move 6, then 3d4+4. On hit: poisoned (healing ends)

lastStand.text: (20): At 0 HP, Pasketti is defeated. 20 more damage and Narbles is defeated. Until then each turn: Move 8, then: Bonk. 2d4+4. On crit: Dazed. Then: Stab: 3d4+4. On hit: Poisoned (healing ends)

flavor: One day, Narbles had a stroke of genius. What if he had six arms and three heads? So he got his pals together and devised a way to make it happen: The Mighty Friendstack - as tall as a dwarf, with only a small a fraction of his stability.

tactics.easier: Stab targets that area already poisoned. Skip the immediate turn at Bloodied and Last Stand, if needed.
tactics.harder: When using Stab, always attack targets that are not Poisoned. When you reach Last Stand, Narbles uses the pan more effectively as a shield, giving him H armor instead of M.

groupTraits.name: Nooooo!
groupTraits.text: Whenever an ally within Reach 2 dies, attack once for free.

notes: Name printed with subtitle "(Pasketti and Toads)". Header "lvl 2 Solo Kobold Friendstack", no size printed. Actions labelled "SOLO:". Last Stand printed as "LAST STAND (20):". Flavour taken from the page's intro paragraph; the in-block flavour is placeholder "xx".

name: Cricket & Hamshake
kind: Kobold & his huge hill giant pal
actionsIntro: Legendary Duo: After each player’s turn choose Cricket or Hamshake to act (rec. alternate).

bloodied.text: If either are reduced below half HP, the other will Interpose for them 1/round.

lastStand.name: NOOOOO!
lastStand.text: If either is killed, the other attacks each turn instead and always attacks with advantage.

tactics.easier: Have Cricket attack more often than Hamshake. Allow the duo to separate a good distance from each other, making Interposing harder.
tactics.harder: Have Hamshake attack more often than Cricket. Keep the duo together, for easier Interposing.

groupTraits.name: Nooooo!
groupTraits.text: Whenever an ally within Reach 2 dies, attack once for free.

notes: Two creatures in one block with separate HP; no size token (Cricket is a kobold, Hamshake a huge hill giant), size left at default. Flavour is placeholder "xx".

name: Pixie
flavor: Tricksters of the forest, flickering in and out of sight at will. Make sure to bring a gift if you ever venture into the borderland of the woods, or hear giggling from the barn.

groupTraits.name: Flutter & Feint
groupTraits.text: Attackers have disadvantage and miss on 2 or less.

notes: No tactics in the block; family-wide "Tiny Fey Tactics" apply: easier "Stay in melee range of the Heroes, especially those rolling larger damage dice or those with AoE abilities." harder "Move out of melee range after attacking. Go after heroes with smaller damage dice."

name: Faerie
flavor: Tiny, mischievous winged humanoids that go about their jokes and schemes with boundless enthusiasm. Being the butt of their jokes is often exhausting, and sometimes dangerous.

groupTraits.name: Flutter & Feint
groupTraits.text: Attackers have disadvantage and miss on 2 or less.

notes: No tactics in the block; family-wide "Tiny Fey Tactics" apply: easier "Stay in melee range of the Heroes, especially those rolling larger damage dice or those with AoE abilities." harder "Move out of melee range after attacking. Go after heroes with smaller damage dice."

name: Faerie Troubadour

traits.name: Invigorating Presence
traits.text: (Reach 4) Fey gain Med armor and advantage on attacks.

actions.name: Clamorous Chorus
actions.text: (Reach 4) Enemies make a WIL save, each takes 15 psychic damage minus the save.

flavor: Faeries love music. The troubadour plays their discordant tunes whenever mischief is underway, escalating whatever chaos other Faeries are causing nearby.

tactics.easier: Isolate yourself from other Fey to limit your boons.
tactics.harder: Stay near allies to grant them additional survivability.

groupTraits.name: Flutter & Feint
groupTraits.text: Attackers have disadvantage and miss on 2 or less.

name: Faerie Merrymaker

actions.name: Prank Bomb
actions.text:
(Range 4) 2d4+10. On hit, choose 1:
• Sticky Gum: Slowed for 1 Round.
• Smelly Gas: Poisoned for 1 Round.

flavor: The merrymaker specialize in practical jokes, and are never seen without their bag of tricks. Watch your step!

tactics.easier: Choose Sticky Gum vs Ranged heroes.
tactics.harder: Combo Smelly Gas with Faerie Troubadour's Clamorous Chorus.

groupTraits.name: Flutter & Feint
groupTraits.text: Attackers have disadvantage and miss on 2 or less.

name: Faerie Trickmage

traits.name: Stop Hitting Yourselves!
traits.text: Reaction, 1/Round. (Reach 4) Swap the position of two creatures.

actions.name: Illusory Assault
actions.text: (Reach 4) Create 3 illusory fey minions (d4) in empty spaces adjacent to a hero. They attack immediately.

actions.name: Minions & Advantage
actions.text: If a minion would attack with advantage, increment their die one step instead.

flavor: Trickmages use illusion magic to drag passers-by into the convoluted plots, often hiding their true motives until the final act. "The more elaborate the setup, the better the punchline."

tactics.easier: Swap positions with your minions.
tactics.harder: Swap positions so the Heroes hit each other with attacks, and focus your minions one one Hero.

groupTraits.name: Flutter & Feint
groupTraits.text: Attackers have disadvantage and miss on 2 or less.

notes: "Minions & Advantage" is an italic boxed note under Illusory Assault, not a separate action.

name: Sprite

traits.name: Spritely Evasion
traits.text: Attackers have disadvantage and miss on 2 or less.

actions.name: Giggle
actions.text: (Reach 4) 1d4. Your next attack deals a max of 1 damage.

flavor: Minor fey that appear to mortals as a winged ball of light. Often seen at dusk fluttering by the streams, groves or meadows to which they are bound.

tactics.easier: Stay in melee with Heroes.
tactics.harder: Attack at max Reach and move each turn.

name: Forest Gnome

traits.name: Weeee!
traits.text: When Riding a creature, attacks are made against you with disadvantage, and any that miss you damage them.

flavor: Amongst the smallest of the forest residents, living peacefully in small communes alongside their critter friends. They do not tolerate rude guests, however.

tactics.easier: Leap off a target after 1 round.
tactics.harder: Ride and attack the same target as long as possible.

notes: Header "lvl 1, small" is partly hidden behind the quote in the page image; confirmed from the text layer.

name: Satyr

traits.name: Revel!
traits.text: When you crit leap 3.

flavor: Satyrs roam the woodland realm in small bands, always looking for a new place to revel. One should be wary of partaking in their merriment, lest they wake, unable to find the way home.

tactics.easier: Leap away from ranged heroes, do not leap away from melee-focused heroes.
tactics.harder: Stay adjacent to ranged heroes making them move or attack with disadvantage; or leap away from melee-focused heroes to make them spend actions moving.

name: Faerie Dragon

traits.name: Iridescent Glamor
traits.text: Attacks deal a max of 10 damage against you. The attacker takes any remaining damage

actions.name: Enchanting Touch
actions.text: 2d6 (ignoring Defense), on hit: target follows you this turn. OR:

flavor: Mages seek out the Faeries Dragons as the most powerful familiar one can court. Highly intelligent, they are silent and communicate through telepathy. They are pure magic, born from the ley-currents of the forest and only found if they wish it so.

tactics.easier: Focus on unarmored Heroes, and use Liminal Breath on one or two targets.
tactics.harder: Use Enchanting Touch to separate a heavily armored heroes from the party, setup a long Centaur charge, or to group heroes together for Liminal Breath

name: Centaur

traits.name: Charge
traits.text: Deal +1 damage for each space you moved toward your target this turn.

flavor: Proud hunters of the forest, reclusive and nomadic. While herds of centaurs can be found all over the world, those dwelling amongst the fey insist on their role as protectors of the forest and its inhabitants. Distrustful of strangers, one would be wise to bring proof of great deeds to earn their esteem.

tactics.easier: Stay in melee combat after charging in.
tactics.harder: Maximize the distance you Charge each turn.

name: Unicorn

traits.name: Iridescent Glamor
traits.text: Attacks deal a max of 10 damage against you. The attacker takes any remaining damage

actions.name: Luminous Horn
actions.text: (If crit this round) d44 damage. Target gains advantage on their next roll.

bloodied.text: (50hp): Can use Luminous Horn freely. (1/round) Radiant Beauty. The nearest other creature Interposes for them on a failed DC 15 WIL save.

flavor: Unicorns are beings of light made manifest, believed to have been sent by the moon itself as guardians of the deep forest. Once abundant when the world was young, they now only reveal themselves to those of pure intent.

tactics.easier: Stay near other monsters and have them Interpose for you instead of a Hero.
tactics.harder: Use Luminous Horn at every opportunity. Stay near a Hero, to use Radiant Beauty on them.

notes: "d44 damage" is printed as-is (possibly a typo).

name: Will-o-Wisp

traits.name: Vanish
traits.text: (1/round, Reach 12) when damaged, teleport.

actions.name: Lure
actions.text: (Reach 12) DC 13 WIL save or move a target 4 spaces and deal them 10 psychic damage. 2 spaces and 5 damage on save.

flavor: The Unseelie counterpart to the Sprite, appearing as ghastly orbs of light floating above swamps and bogs. Their ethereal allure has brought many a wanderer to a watery grave.

tactics.easier: When hit, teleport near another Hero. Use Lure to move Heroes without purpose.
tactics.harder: When hit, teleport out of melee/movement range. Use Lure to separate the party, with hazards, or set up stronger monster attacks, like a Nixie in water.

name: Brollachan

traits.name: Look-not-at-me
traits.text: Heroes can choose to close their eyes and be Blinded, otherwise you spend one of their actions each round.

flavor: A formless creature of shadow that covets the shape worn by others. It enters the eyes of fools who stare at it too long, taking possession of their form until their bodies succumb or their will is spent.

tactics.easier: Use the target’s action to attack higher armor Heroes.
tactics.harder: Use the target’s action to move them next to a stronger monster, like a Bogey, a Nixie in water, or to deal damage to a weaker Hero.

notes: Flavour and tactics continue at the top of the next column.

name: Nixie

traits.name: Waterbound
traits.text: Moving on land is difficult terrain.

actions.name: Abduct
actions.text: 1d8, Grappled (escape DC 13 or lightning damage ends). OR:

actions.name: Drown
actions.text: (target in water) 2d8+10, Grappled, Silenced, and suffer 1 Wound each round (escape DC 13 or lightning damage ends).

flavor: Solitary watchers found in still bodies of water. They play dreadfully enchanting music on unseen instruments to draw the weak-hearted to their demise, calling out for companionship they can never grasp.

tactics.easier: Leave the water to chase down heroes.
tactics.harder: If possible, stay in the water and have other monsters (Brollican, Will-o-Wisp, or Bogey) bring targets to you,

notes: Harder tactic ends with a comma in the source.

name: Redcap

traits.name: Murderous Mayhem
traits.text: The Redcap suffers 10 damage each round it fails to deal damage.

flavor: Often mistaken for a forest gnomes, these vile and murderous fey delight in violence, and get their names from their habit of soaking their caps in the blood of their victims.

tactics.easier: Use Iron Boots, even against Prone creatures. Target high defense heroes
tactics.harder: Many Redcaps can gang up on a single target.

name: Jabberwocky

traits.name: Mad Babbling
traits.text: Initiative is a WIL save instead. 1-9: the Jabberwocky can make you perform 2 actions this round, 10-19: 1 action (this does not spend any existing actions).

actions.name: Eyes of Flame
actions.text: (Reach 12, max 1 target). 2d10. Target takes this damage again at the end of their turn until extinguished (if the Jabberwocky is crit, water is used, or spending an action dropping Prone and rolling ends).

bloodied.text: At 120 hp use Mad Babbling again, all heroes roll with disadvantage.

flavor: Jabberwockies are false dragons that babble incessantly, drawing in their prey with a maddening allure. Gazing too long into its eyes is said to reveal both the true shape of the world, and the incomprehensible horror in the space behind it.

tactics.easier: Use actions from Mad Babbling to move Heroes randomly, and attack each other. Use Claws That Catch more often.
tactics.harder: Use actions from Mad Babbling to set up attacks for other monsters, such as Bogeys and Nixies, and to attack or interpose against each other. Use Jaws that Bite more often.

name: Gremlin

traits.name: Come Get Some!
traits.text: If no heroes are Taunted, you may Taunt ALL heroes for 1 Round.

flavor: Diminutive troublemakers with a craving for chaos and disorder. No two gremlins are alike, their patterns of fur and horns as varied as the targets of their vexation.

tactics.easier: Taunt melee heroes that are near you.
tactics.harder: Taunt with a Gremlin that is further away or behind cover and not riding a hero; this makes all attacks against riding Gremlins made with disadvantage and more likely to hit the hero they're riding!

name: Gremlin Wrestler

traits.name: Come Get Some!
traits.text: If no heroes are Taunted, you may Taunt all heroes for 1 Round.

traits.name: Punching Up
traits.text: Can Grapple Med/Large creatures.

actions.name: I’mma Mess You Up!
actions.text: 2d6+10. On hit: Grappled (escape DC 12). If Grappled, knock Prone as well.

flavor: Nasty bullies who immobilize much larger opponents with a mix of innate physical strength and fey magic.

tactics.easier: Switch from hero to hero, abstain from knocking Prone.
tactics.harder: Focus on one hero, knock Prone as much as possible. Always Taunt with the highest HP gremlin to protect those who are lower on HP.

notes: Harder tactic continues onto printed page 23.

name: Gremlin Roastmaster

traits.name: Take a look at this tough guy!
traits.text: (Reach 6) Heroes that miss attacks suffer 5 psychic damage.

flavor: Gremlins notorious enough to lead their own gang of bullies through insults and intimidation. Always on the lookout for new victims to strengthen their vile reputation.

tactics.easier: Limit "Take a look at this tough guy!" to 1/round.
tactics.harder: Stay near the heroes that are attacking taunting Gremlins to activate “Take a look at this tough guy!” as often as possible. Focus your Cheap Shots on heroes that are being hampered by Wrestlers.

name: Bogey

traits.name: Taste for Violence
traits.text: If a Bogey has 2 or more adjacent heroes, it uses a d20 for its attacks.

flavor: Distant cousins of Gremlins. Their lanky, hulking forms bely their cunning nature. Unlike most Fey, Bogeys are overtly malicious, taking cruel satisfaction in the pain and sadness of those they lure into the dark.

tactics.easier: Focus on isolated heroes.
tactics.harder: Stay near groups of heroes to maximize damage.

notes: Printed in the Gremlins section; described as distant cousins of Gremlins.

name: Gremlin Minion

actions.name: Bully
actions.text: 1d6 (1d8 instead vs a Blinded or Ridden target).

notes: Printed alongside Razzle, Gremlin Iconoclast.

name: Razzle, Gremlin Iconoclast

traits.name: "The Boys."
traits.text: When combat begins, 2 Gremlin minions/hero arrive as well.

traits.name: Endless Stream of Vile Insults
traits.text: All heroes are permanently Taunted by Razzle.

actions.name: Get ‘em Boys!
actions.text: (If no minions died last turn) All minions move then attack.

actions.name: Poke Eyes, Pull Hair
actions.text: (If a minion died last turn) Teleport to an enemy, gain Riding and attack for 1d6+6. On hit: Blinded 1 round. Then (if the heroes outnumber the gremlins) summon 1 minion/hero.

bloodied.name: “Razzle Dazzle!”
bloodied.text: At 90 HP A flash of glitter Blinds all heroes for 1 round. Razzle may teleport 8 and summon 1 minion/hero.

lastStand.text: At 0 HP, Razzle is losing his cool! 70 more damage and he’s banished to the Wildscapes. 3 Gremlin Minions/hero arrive to protect him. Razzle turns invisible until the end of the next Hero's turn.

tactics.easier: Have your minions spread out and attack many different heroes. Summon fewer minions when Bloodied and at his Last Stand.
tactics.harder: Have minions prioritize Blinded and Ridden heroes for more damage. Increment the damage die on all his minions from d6 to d10.

notes: Header "Level 7 Small, Insufferable Rascal" does not say Solo, but the block uses ACTIONS/BLOODIED/LAST STAND, so role set to solo. No flavour paragraph in the block; lore, quest hook and quips are on the surrounding page.

name: Mav, The Winter Queen

traits.name: Ice Avatar
traits.text: Resistant to Ice, vulnerable to Fire: when dealt Fire damage, her next attack is made with advantage.

traits.name: Wind Ward
traits.text: Attacks from Range 6 or beyond have disadvantage against Mav.

actionsIntro: After each hero’s turn choose 1 (Rec. use Winter's Wrath as an opening move):

actions.name: Winter’s Wrath
actions.text: (1 use, remains until Last Stand) Create a 6x6 area of wintry storm within Reach 8. Enemies in the area take 10 damage. They take 10 more whenever they enter the area and if they end their turn there.

actions.name: Wolf-Spirit’s Bite
actions.text: Move 10, 1d10+8. Drag target 2 spaces in any direction.

actions.name: Stormlord’s Gust
actions.text: (Reach 8) All heroes make a DC 15 STR Save. Move all heroes that fail up to 4 spaces in the same direction; on success, half as far.

bloodied.text: At 140 HP, Mav’s Winter's Wrath increases to 8x8. Mav is no longer vulnerable to Fire. Your forced movement moves twice as far.

lastStand.text: At 0 HP, Mav is thawing out! 100 more damage and she’s banished to the Wildscapes. Her WInter's Wrath is ended, Mav summons icy shards that cover the ground within Reach 12. Enemies suffer 3 damage for each space they move in the area.

tactics.easier: Stray outside of your Winter’s Wrath, preventing heroes from taking damage in it. Her Wind Ward could falter after taking a crit, or Fire damage. Icy shards can deal less damage or be destroyed once used.
tactics.harder: Stay within Winter’s Wrath and make the heroes come to you. Drag and push heroes into the storm. Keep ranged attackers outside of your Wind Ward. At Last Stand, use Stormlord’s Gust to more heroes across as many shards as possible.

notes: Header "Level 10 Solo Avatar of Seasons"; actions labelled "SOLO:". No flavour paragraph in the block; lore, quest hook and quotes are on the page.
